title: Three Spoons, Then This: Alex Baker Takes the Trophy at Camiral
title_candidates: Three Spoons, Then This: Alex Baker Takes the Trophy at Camiral
A Hundred and Six, and Still Eleven Clear
The Wheel Turns in Girona: Spoon-Holder in the Jacket, Champion in the Spoon
Forty-Six on the First Afternoon: How the Trophy Was Won Before Anyone Noticed
theme: The order turned upside down at Camiral: the man with three Wooden Spoons won the Trophy, the reigning Spoon-holder won the Green Jacket, and the defending champion took the Spoon — and all of it was settled amid the biggest collection of double figures TEG has produced in some time. The winner didn't avoid the wreckage; he was simply the one whose wreckage cost him least.
tone: house — faithful, entertaining, tongue-in-cheek; Ronay/Peck register, anchored in the facts and gently merciless with the principals
opening_hook: Open on Alex Baker in R2 signing for 106 at the Tour course — the worst gross round in 22 TEG visits there (cr02), an 11 at the last (b44) — and still leading the Trophy by 11. That single image contains the whole report: the champion who was never troubled and never remotely tidy. Then organise the body by idea (how the Trophy was won on the first afternoon / how Williams rebuilt from the rubble / how the defending champion sank / the catalogue of big numbers) rather than by plain chronology.
foreshadow: Alex Baker arrives with three prior Wooden Spoons and the Spoon in two of the last three TEGs — the least likely name on the trophy
Gregg Williams arrives as the reigning Wooden Spoon holder (TEG 17) and opens with a 9 at the 7th and an 8 at the 17th (b30, b28)
Jon Baker arrives as defending Trophy AND Jacket champion, and leads the gross after both rounds on the Tour course
R1's 15th at the Tour course: Mullin makes 11 and drops to the bottom of the Spoon race (b46, b68) while Alex Baker birdies it for five points (b50) — one hole, two directions

competitions.name: Trophy (Stableford)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Alex Baker (169 pts, by 8 from John Patterson)
competitions.how: Won in a single afternoon and then defended by simply existing. A best-in-field 46 in R1 (b47, b50) put 12 points between him and Patterson; the outright lead taken at R1 H5 was never surrendered over the remaining 67 holes. The margin went 12 → 11 → 12 → 8, so every point of the eventual winning margin — and four more besides — came from day one: across R2-R4 Patterson actually outscored him by four. A second best-in-field round in R3 (44 pts, b10) killed the only realistic move against him. The blow-ups (cr02, b44, b34) were spectacular and, in Stableford terms, nearly free.

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Gregg Williams (+66, by 14 from David Mullin)
competitions.how: The only competition genuinely built rather than inherited. Williams was third and below field median after an R1 littered with a 9 and an 8 (b30, b28), rescued by a birdie at the 15th (b37); he answered with the best round in the field in R2 (b41, 42 pts / 86 gross), drew level at R2 H13 (b36), then went outright clear at R3 H2 (b39) and never looked back — 8 clear after R3, 14 after R4. The close was ruthless: 13 holes in R4 without dropping a net shot (b01) for 84 gross, a personal best at the Stadium by eight shots. He outscored Mullin in three of four rounds.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.winner_or_loser: Jon Baker (126 pts, 23 adrift of David Mullin)
competitions.how: Lost comprehensively and from the front. The defending champion led the Jacket after R1 and R2 (b38), then produced nothing on the Stadium: below the field median in all four rounds, a 9 at the 4th in R3 (b49), 28 and 29 points in the last two rounds. The decisive round was R3, where Mullin's course-record 84 (cr01) took 16 points out of him in one afternoon and turned a scrap into a formality. Only R2's 39 points — a birdie at the 14th and eight clean closing holes (b13, b16) — suggested a man who had won both pots twelve months earlier.

headline_candidates: Forty-Six on Saturday: The Trophy Effectively Signed For at the Tour Course
Carnage in Girona, and One Man Quietly Counting Points
Patterson Drops 22 in Eight, Mullin Makes 11, Baker Makes 46
rounds.chosen_headline: Forty-Six on Saturday: The Trophy Effectively Signed For at the Tour Course
rounds.angle: While the rest of the field dismantled itself — Patterson bleeding 22 shots in eight holes, Mullin's 11 at the 15th, Williams's 9 and 8 — Alex Baker took the lead at the 5th and posted 46, twelve clear. Nobody was ever that close to him again.

headline_candidates: A Hundred and Six, and Still Eleven Clear
The Course Worst That Cost Its Owner Nothing
An 11 at the Last, a Record at the Wrong End, a Lead Intact
rounds.chosen_headline: A Hundred and Six, and Still Eleven Clear
rounds.angle: Alex Baker posts the worst gross round in 22 TEG visits to the Tour course (cr02), signs off with an 11 at the 18th (b44) — and loses precisely one point of his lead. Behind him, Williams answers his R1 with the best round in the field, and Jon Baker's 39 keeps him top of the gross for one more day.

rounds.chosen_headline: Eighty-Four at the Stadium: Mullin Breaks the Record, Williams Takes the Jacket
rounds.angle: The best round anyone has played at the Stadium in 27 prior TEG visits (cr01) and it wins its author nothing but pride — while Williams goes outright ahead on gross at the 2nd (b39) and Jon Baker's 9 at the 4th sends him to the bottom for good.

headline_candidates: A Ten at the Fourteenth, and the Trophy Anyway
Thirteen Clean Holes: Williams Finishes the Job in the Jacket
Baker Beats Baker: One Trophy, One Spoon, One Surname
rounds.chosen_headline: A Ten at the Fourteenth, and the Trophy Anyway
rounds.angle: Alex Baker's last act of vandalism (b34) is irrelevant because the work was done on day one; Williams closes with 13 holes without dropping a net shot (b01) and a Stadium personal best for the Jacket by 14; Jon Baker collects the Spoon he has been holding since R3.

players.arc: Three Wooden Spoons and two of the last three TEGs spent at the bottom, and he wins the Trophy by eight while also setting the worst gross round in the Tour course's TEG history — the whole margin banked in a 46-point opener and never seriously threatened.

Reigning Wooden Spoon holder, opens with a 9 and an 8 and sits below the field median, then plays the best round in the field twice and closes with a Stadium personal best of 84 to take the Green Jacket by 14 — the only prize this TEG that was genuinely built rather than left lying around.

Defending champion of both Trophy and Jacket, leads the gross for two days, then goes below the field median in all four rounds and hands his own brother the family bragging rights while collecting the Spoon by 23.

Personal bests at both Catalunya courses, outscored the champion in two of four rounds, and still finished eight adrift — because on day one he lost 22 shots in eight holes and spent three days paying it back at the wrong exchange rate.

An 11 at the 15th in R1 that dropped him to the bottom of the Spoon race, then the lowest round in the Stadium's TEG history (84, a course record) in R3 — nine Jackets already on the peg and this time he finished second in that too, 14 back.

venue_notes: TEG's 4th visit to Catalonia and by now thoroughly familiar ground: R1-R2 on the Tour course (its 5th and 6th TEG rounds), R3-R4 on the Stadium (6th and 7th). Play the two courses as different examinations — the 'slightly more forgiving' Tour course somehow produced the tournament's biggest scorecard vandalism (a 106, two 11s, three quadruple bogeys), while Spain's premier championship layout gave up a new TEG course record (84) and two personal bests. Girona in October, Camiral's parkland, and a resort that has now seen 49 TEG rounds' worth of evidence about these five men.
course_history_notes: Mullin's 6th visit to the Stadium produced a new personal best of 84 in R3 — seven better than his prior best of 91 (TEG 11), eight better than his last visit, and a new TEG course record across 27 prior visits (cr01).

Williams's 6th visit to the Stadium also produced an 84, in R4 — eight better than his prior best of 92 (TEG 12) and eight better than his last visit; the round that turned a Jacket lead into a 14-shot rout.
Patterson set personal bests at BOTH courses — 94 at the Tour in R2 and 93 at the Stadium in R3 — and still lost the Trophy by eight.

The two men at either end of the Trophy went backwards on familiar ground: Alex Baker was seven shots worse at the Stadium than his last visit (best 100 v a prior best of 93), and Jon Baker eight worse (97 v a prior best of 89 from TEG 12).
decisive_moments: Trophy: R1 at the Tour course — Alex Baker takes the outright lead at the 5th, signs for 46 points and a 12-point cushion, and is never headed across the remaining 67 holes; every point of the eventual eight-shot margin was banked before dinner on Saturday.

Green Jacket: R3 H2 at the Stadium (b39) — Williams goes outright ahead of Jon Baker on gross for the first time and converts a two-shot deficit into an eight-shot lead by the end of the round, then 14 by the end of R4.

Wooden Spoon: R3 at the Stadium — Jon Baker's 9 at the 4th (b49) and 28 points against Mullin's course-record 84 (cr01) costs him 16 points in a single round and turns a live scrap into a 23-point formality.

payoffs.payoff: He wins the Trophy by eight on 169 points (b03) — the second-best score of his TEG career and a second Trophy — the underdog frame closing on the man previously best known for finishing last.

payoffs.seed: Williams the reigning Spoon-holder opening with a 9 and an 8 in R1
payoffs.payoff: Birdie at the 15th stops the bleeding (b37), the best round in the field follows in R2 (b41), the Jacket lead is taken at R3 H2 (b39) and sealed with 13 clean net holes and a Stadium personal best of 84 in R4 (b01, b02) — Spoon to Jacket in twelve months.

payoffs.seed: Jon Baker, defending champion of both pots, leading the gross after R1 and R2
payoffs.payoff: He loses the gross lead at R3 H2, makes 9 at the 4th (b49), goes below the field median in all four rounds and collects the Spoon on 126 points (b29) — 23 adrift, with his brother holding the Trophy.

payoffs.seed: R1's 15th at the Tour course: Mullin's 11 (b46, b68) alongside Alex Baker's birdie (b50)
payoffs.resolves_in: The catalogue of big numbers (closing thematic section)
payoffs.payoff: Inventory the double figures and quadruple bogeys — Mullin's 11, Alex Baker's 11 and 10 (b44, b34), Williams's 9 and 8 (b30, b28), Patterson's two 8s (b31, b24), Jon Baker's 9 (b49) — and land the point: the champion owned two of the worst of them, including a course-worst 106 (cr02), and it changed nothing, because handicap golf punishes consistency of failure, not the size of any single crater.

vehicle_fit_response.note: Taken up as a supporting frame — the blow-up inventory is genuinely the connective tissue of this TEG (a 106 course-worst, two 11s, a 10, a 9 and a clutch of 8s) — but it rides behind 'underdog', because the story is a three-time Spoon-collector holding the Trophy.

why_the_champion_won: Alex Baker won it in one afternoon and then refused to lose it: a best-in-field 46 in R1 opened a 12-point gap that was larger than the eventual eight-point margin, a second best-in-field round in R3 killed the only counter-move, and the narrowest round-to-round spread in the field (8 against a field median of 11) meant Patterson — who actually outscored him across R2-R4 by four, and who could not have flipped it even by replacing his worst round with his own average — was always chasing a debt run up before he had settled in.
